objective: Coordinator's pick (18 November 2026), KNOT-CAP-20261117-001's second direction: why do presentations of the same line by betweenness knots (the line of five with its shared distinction at an end, next to an end or in the middle; the six-starts) grow different numbers of orders under the knot-local fewest-states rule KF3? Find an invariant of how the knots meet that predicts the order distribution, prove what can be proved, cover the untested next-to-end position, and say whether the six-starts' agreement through n = 9 follows from the same mechanism. Serves G1 and G16; tests A97.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; referee pending): what the states do not carry is the bracketing, which knot lies within which half of which; the fewest-knot presentations of a line are exactly its bracketings, and under KF3 the chance of two orders after the second new distinction is an exact function of the bare bracketing (proved; 5/12 for chains, the end and next-to-end placements, 11/18 for the middle, 51/140 for both six-starts); the bare bracketing decides the whole distribution through the third new distinction (computed, every presentation of 5 to 9), the halves enter at the fourth (next to an end parts from the end at n = 9, the six-starts at 10); post hoc the meeting pattern alone decides how the growth branches. 6 of 8 predictions held; one Not-a-block correction to KNOT-CAP.
stop_rule: One proof and one frozen computation with its read-out; A97 status; referee hand-off; report.
title: Why how the knots meet changes the number of orders
